summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with a two-week history of abdominal distention, nausea, poor appetite, and constipation, with a single episode of vomiting on the day of admission. She has a complex medical history including chronic graft-versus-host disease, gastroparesis, and chronic opiate use for back pain. Abdominal X-ray revealed fecal loading, supporting constipation as a primary contributor to her symptoms. She was treated with an enema and bowel prep, which resolved her nausea and improved her abdominal discomfort. She underwent an EGD and colonoscopy, which revealed gastric nodules and a colonic ulcer with inflammation; biopsies were taken to evaluate for medication effects, infection, or GVHD. Dicyclomine was discontinued, metoclopramide was increased, and she was discharged on daily Miralax to prevent recurrence. She tolerated oral intake, remained stable, and was discharged home in improved condition with plans to follow up on biopsy results and with her GI specialist.
